source_review.notes: Checked current AMD and Intel timing-analysis and closure guidance, the primary OpenSTA repository, the current IEEE SystemVerilog record, author resources for digital architecture, and a current publisher record for CMOS VLSI design. All eight authoritative URLs returned HTTP 200. Tool semantics, constraint methodology, simplified timing arithmetic, implementation practices and physical recommendations remain separately scoped.

evidence: Checked clock period/frequency, maximum/minimum clock-to-Q and combinational delay, setup/hold, uncertainty, arrival, required-time and slack notation.
Verified setup and hold use separate latest/earliest obligations and declared sign conventions.
notation_and_syntax.notes: Notation distinguishes data and clock paths, maximum and minimum analysis, simplified lumped equations and tool-specific graph propagation.

evidence: Recomputed minimum period as 70+530+80+50 = 730 ps and frequency as 1000/730 = 1.370 GHz.
Recomputed earliest hold arrival as 45 ps, requirement as 55 ps and hold slack as -10 ps.
numerical_recomputation.notes: The deterministic Python snippet reproduced all seven expected timing values and status outputs.

evidence: Re-derived the simplified setup lower bound from launch clock-to-Q, maximum data delay, endpoint setup and uncertainty.
Re-derived hold slack from earliest data arrival minus minimum required stability and confirmed clock period does not enter the same-edge simplified relation.
symbolic_recomputation.notes: The equations omit propagated clock arrival, edge phase, derates, slew/load tables and variation; the chapter labels them as scaffolding.

evidence: Reviewed missing clocks, unconstrained endpoints, incorrect generated phases, absent I/O minimums, broad false paths, multicycle hold errors and asynchronous crossings.
Reviewed fanout, slew, interconnect, congestion, PVT, OCV, voltage domains, hold ECOs, useful skew, retiming reset, low-power/test modes and silicon outliers.
boundary_and_adversarial_cases.notes: Clock, data, interface, exception, CDC, library, physical, mode, corner and correlation boundaries receive distinct treatment.

evidence: Traced architectural period and interface budgets through clock definitions, graph start/end points, arrivals, required times and slack.
Verified endpoint coverage, max/min corners, exception proof, pipeline alignment, ECO regression and exact artifact identity.
invariant_checking.notes: The invariant set prevents a clean report with missing constraints or incorrect exceptions from qualifying as timing closure.

evidence: Reviewed fifteen architecture, clock, coverage, setup, hold, crossing, exception, corner, physical, pipeline, ECO, report, evidence, correlation and change obligations.
Constructed counterexamples for gate-count-as-criticality, lower-frequency-as-hold-fix, false-path-as-CDC, no-violations-as-full-coverage and pre-layout-as-sign-off claims.
proof_review.notes: The chapter supplies conditional timing obligations, not formal proof of constraint correctness, library characterization, tool implementation, silicon or system performance.

evidence: Audited uses of critical, maximum, minimum, closed, constrained, false, multicycle, safe, worst and sign-off.
Confirmed architectural targets, model bounds, tool reports, exceptions, physical extraction, silicon observations and residual margins remain separate.
proof_sketch_labeling.notes: The calculated frequency is explicitly a simplified path limit rather than maximum chip frequency or silicon guarantee.

evidence: artifacts/snippets/CA-008/report.json records source, expected and actual output, stderr, exit status, Python toolchain and environment for setup/hold arithmetic.
Reviewed required clocks, I/O budgets, exceptions, modes, corners, libraries, netlist, parasitics, reports, waivers, silicon samples and measurement-limit evidence.
empirical_evidence_labeling.notes: The passing toy establishes seven arithmetic outputs only; it provides no evidence for an STA graph, real clock, extracted path, process corner or silicon frequency.

conceptual_review.notes: Reviewed timing as a constrained launch-to-capture graph whose latest and earliest paths, clocks, interfaces, exceptions and physical variation jointly support synchronous behavior.

practitioner_review.notes: Reviewed implementable concerns including clocks, I/O delays, setup, hold, skew, jitter, false/multicycle paths, CDC, libraries, PVT/OCV, wires, slew, fanout, pipelining, retiming, ECOs, reports and silicon correlation. Internal practitioner-oriented review only.

pedagogical_review.notes: Verified progression from timing graphs and equations through complete constraints and physical analysis to closure and governance, followed by fifteen obligations, fifteen trade-offs, twenty-six misconceptions, ten examples and five complete exercises.

limitations: Internal evidence record only; no external computer-architecture academic, STA or library specialist, FPGA or ASIC timing-closure engineer, clock-tree or physical-design expert, silicon-characterization reviewer, medical safety assessor, independent-verification or certification review is claimed.
